newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after PPI.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - U.S. stocks seen up after PPI.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen opening higher after the release of the January Producer Price Index, analysts said.
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER OF VALUE LINE'S ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION:
-- "Bonds are going to soar and this market will soar. Not only is inflation not a concern, but we are still getting excellent corporate earnings."

-- "The Fed's March meeting should focus on whether they should cut rates rather than raise them. Based on this number, it appears we are now in a deflationary environment. Bonds and equity should continue to rally on this news."
The PPI in January fell 0.3 percent, marking its first drop since October 1994. Excluding the volatile food an energy components, it was unchanged.
Economists in a Reuters poll had expected the PPI to rise 0.3 percent after a revised 0.6 percent rise in December.
HUGH JOHNSON, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER AT FIRST ALBANY:

-- "Whoosh! It almost leaves you speechless. It doesn't say much forecasters. Despite the fact that economy has been recovering since March of 1991, there are still are very few signs of upward pressure on prices. That's very, very unusual."

-- "This will touch off a very strong opening. I think to a great extent we will sustain it. There is likely to be profit-taking at midday, but I wouldn't be at all surpised to see the stock market up 30 points at the close, and that's probably a modest estimate."
-- JOHN WOSCZYNA, MARKET STRATEGIST AT RONEY & CO:
-- "The PPI is probably going to help the market in the short run, assisting in what's already been established as far as an uptrend."
